title: Machine learning-based analysis of distribution characteristics and sensitivity of soil organic carbon in typical soils of China
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is a vital component of the terrestrial ecosystem carbon cycle, reducing global warming and promoting plant nutrition, with its changes greatly impacting the global carbon balance and climate change. Recent studies show that different soil types have different abilities to store carbon under the influence of climate, topography, vegetation, and human activities. This study investigates five typical soil types in China (dark brown soil, aeolian soil, alpine meadow soil, red soil, and yellow soil), utilizing an open-access SOC density database and relevant literature to collect SOC density data from 2004 to 2023. Using the Random Forest (RF) model, the SOC density of the 0–20 cm soil layer from 2000 to 2023 was examined to reveal its changes over time and location and influencing factors. The study integrated SOC data from 2000 to 2023 with environmental factors, including climate, topography, vegetation, and soil properties. We found that SOC density across the five soil types ranks as follows: dark brown soil (8.75 kg/m 2 ) > alpine meadow soil (6.59 kg/m 2 ) > yellow soil (5.81 kg/m 2 ) > red soil (4.57 kg/m 2 ) > aeolian soil (2.47 kg/m 2 ). The carbon storage capacity of these soil types is influenced by factors like climate, vegetation, and soil properties. Furthermore, SHAP analysis revealed how each soil type responds differently to these factors. Based on these findings, we propose strategies for managing soil carbon storage. For different soil types, we recommend measures like restoring plant cover, using conservation tillage, and increasing tree planting to boost carbon storage and align with the dual carbon goals of China to tackle climate change. • A database of SOC for five typical soil types in China from 2015 to 2023(Manually collected). • Significant differences in carbon storage capacity among five typical soils. • The key factors influencing the carbon storage capacity of five typical soil types in China were quantified. • Revealed the threshold effects of key factors on the carbon sequestration capacity of five typical soil.

title: Hybrid machine learning solutions for mitigating climate-induced productivity losses in sustainable construction management
abstract: Climate change has contributed to increased weather extremes, which require new and proactive planning and workforce management practices in construction. This research created a hybrid machine learning model (HMLM) using XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost to predict construction worker productivity across a variety of weather conditions. We trained these models for a decade-long dataset capturing daily weather parameters and productivity in U.S. construction sites. The ensemble methods were able to reduce the root mean square error (RMSE) to 4.50, a 10 % improvement over the best single model. Using the RCP 8.5 scenario, our analysis predicts substantial effects upon construction productivity due to climate change. The SHAP analysis showed that precipitation and temperature together contributed 15 % of the model’s total mean absolute SHAP importance on the test set, indicating their strong model-based influence on predicted productivity (not causation). On top of this, our findings showcase that temperature fluctuations from 15 °C to 35 °C and humidity from 40 % to 70 % could impact productivity by 7.5 %, while productivity under ideal conditions could be at 92.5 %. Accordingly, the understanding of these events used in project management has shown reductions in delays of up to 30 days while in adverse situations. A strong implementation of such a concept is found in this research showing how a construction firm could improve workforce performance and project duration by adapting for climate, and producing data-informed decision making by as much as 25 % -this research strongly advocates for a proactive management process around climate variability and uncertainty.

title: Towards cleaner production of methyl glycolate: Techno-economic-environmental optimization via hybrid physics-machine learning modeling
abstract: The transition to sustainable chemical manufacturing requires a balance among technical feasibility, economic viability, and environmental impact. This challenge is particularly evident in the dimethyl oxalate to methyl glycolate (DTMG) process, a promising route for producing a key monomer of biodegradable polymers. To address these, this study develops a hybrid physics-machine learning framework for multi-objective optimization (HyMeO) of the DTMG process. It seamlessly integrates the strengths of process simulation, automated machine learning, and natural heuristic algorithms. A high-fidelity dataset of 1058 operational scenarios is generated via rigorous process simulation. Eight machine learning models are developed and automatically optimized, with the deep neural network model demonstrating the best performance (R2 > 0.96). The Shapley additive explains and partial dependency analyses are conducted to unveil the internal prediction mechanism of this model, which reveal that the distillate-to-feed ratio of the MG refining column and the hydrogen flowrate are the most influential factors governing the trade-offs between economic and environmental objectives. The preferred model coupled with the genetic algorithm to maximize exergy efficiency while minimizing production cost and CO2 emission of the DTMG process. The optimal solution achieves an 8.82 % increase in exergy efficiency, an 8.91 % cost reduction, and a 0.31 % decrease in CO2 emissions. Therefore, the proposed HyMeO framework can effectively reconcile the trade-offs among economic, technical, and environmental objectives in the DTMG process, providing a generalizable methodology for the sustainable intensification of chemical processes.

title: Synergizing artificial neural networks with SSP-RCP scenarios: Long-Term projection of residential electricity demand in China under climate-economic interactions
abstract: Amid escalating climate challenges, understanding the compound effects of economic and climatic drivers on residential electricity demand has become critical for sustainable energy planning. This study develops an integrated modeling framework combining econometric analysis with machine learning to forecast China's residential electricity consumption through 2100. Utilizing provincial-level panel data (2001–2019), we first employ fixed-effects regression to identify significant predictors. The results reveal that both economic variables (including per capita GDP [PGDP] and tertiary industry share [TIS]) and climatic variables (including Cooling/Heating Degree Days [CDD/HDD] and CO2 emissions [CO2]) exhibit statistically significant effects. These determinants are subsequently integrated into an artificial neural network (ANN) architecture enhanced with scenario analysis combining Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) and Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP). Our ANN-SSP-RCP hybrid integration reduces RMSE by 13.16 %–26.83 % versus traditional models by capturing nonlinear climate-economic dynamics. Key projections reveal: (1) Under deep decarbonization scenarios (2020–2060, compared to RCP4.5 and RCP8.5), early-stage decarbonization (RCP2.6) triggers a demand rebound of 1.51 %–2.39 % due to large-scale electrification; (2) By 2100, the impact of climate factors on China's residential electricity demand is 2.7 times greater than the impact of socioeconomic factors; (3) By 2100, residential electricity consumption in the high emissions scenario will be 100 billion kWh higher than in the low emissions scenario. The framework informs adaptive policies for grid resilience, regional energy-sharing, and rebound-effect mitigation, advancing China's dual-carbon targets amid climate-economy synergies across different development trajectories.

title: Algal bloom control through machine learning guided inverse design of pre-oxidation-coagulation
abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) threaten drinking water safety and ecosystem stability. Pre-oxidation–coagulation is an effective control method, but its operational optimization remains challenging due to nonlinear parameter interactions and limited systematic datasets. A machine learning–based inverse design framework was developed to optimize pre-oxidation–coagulation processes for algal removal. Literature data (n = 328) were supplemented with 471 newly conducted orthogonal experiments, yielding a balanced dataset (n = 799) covering nine oxidants, three coagulants, and pre-oxidation times from 5 to 60 min. A stacked ensemble model, employing CatBoost as the meta-learner over four base algorithms, was trained and interpreted using SHAP analysis. The model was coupled with sequential quadratic programming (SQP) for inverse parameter optimization, with target removal efficiency of 90 %. The ensemble model achieved an average test R2 = 0.783, with substantial gains for challenging oxidants such as K2FeO4 (+34.01 %). SHAP analysis ranked parameter importance as coagulant dose > oxidant dose > pre-oxidation time > oxidant type, revealing saturation of pre-oxidation effects within 5–20 min. Inverse design reduced experimental workload by over 98 % (384–6 validation runs) while maintaining ±8.34 % accuracy. Experimental validation (6 triplicate runs) confirmed both predictive reliability and process efficiency. Balanced datasets are critical for capturing oxidation-specific dynamics. The proposed framework offers a cost-effective, data-driven solution for rapid, precise HAB control, bridging laboratory studies with full-scale water treatment operations.

title: Biochar's impact on carbon sequestration and yield-scaled global warming potential in China: A machine learning-enhanced meta-analysis
abstract: Biochar has shown strong potential to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, yet most meta-analyses have examined isolated factors, overlooking the interactive effects of climate, soil, and management on agricultural productivity and environmental sustainability. This study integrated meta-analysis with machine learning (ML) to quantify biochar's effects on GHG emission, soil organic carbon (SOC), and yield-scaled global warming potential (GWP). A total of 1207 paired observations from 64 field studies conducted in China (2000–2024) were analysed. Biochar application significantly increased crop yield by 5 % and SOC by 34 %, while reducing NO emissions by 25 %, resulting in a 25 % decrease in yield-scaled GWP. Weakly alkaline biochar was most effective in reducing CO emissions in alkaline soils and CH emissions in acidic to neutral soils ( p < 0.05). Low C/N ratio biochar significantly decreased CO and CH emissions across soils with varying C/N ratios. Machine learning models identified biochar pH, application rate, soil pH, and soil C/N ratio as the primary determinants of these effects. CO emission responses were positively correlated with biochar application rate and negatively correlated with soil pH and C/N ratio ( p < 0.05), whereas CH emissions were positively regulated by soil pH, soil C/N ratio, and biochar pH. Pathway analysis indicated that biochar pH indirectly reduced CO emissions through enhanced SOC, while soil pH and C/N ratio directly influenced CH dynamics ( p < 0.05). Overall, this study demonstrates biochar's potential to enhance crop productivity while mitigating GHG emissions, providing a scientific basis for its application in carbon-neutral agroecosystems development.

title: Integrating system dynamics and machine learning to establish the Water-Energy-Food-Climate-Land (WEFCL) nexus of aquavoltaics
abstract: Traditional aquaculture faces growing challenges from climate change, including rising water temperatures, reduced water availability, and declining yields. This study explores aquavoltaic systems—integrating aquaculture with solar panels—as a sustainable, climate-resilient solution. We used clam farming at the Mariculture Research Center Taihsi Station in Yunlin County, Taiwan, as a case study. Within the Water-Energy-Food-Climate-Land (WEFCL) nexus framework, we applied system dynamics (SD) modeling enhanced by a hybrid machine learning approach. By combining the genetic algorithm (GA) and the backpropagation neural network (BPNN), we improved the accuracy and reliability of SD models, simulating real-world conditions using in-situ monitoring datasets to promote sustainability, resource use efficiency, and policy coherence in aquaculture. Results show that 40 % solar panel shading reduced water temperatures by 2.5 °C, improved water use efficiency by 30 %, and generated renewable energy to offset emissions. Although clam yields declined by 27 %, solar power compensated for production losses, creating an economically viable system. Further optimization identified 45 % shading as ideal, preserving 70 % of yields while maximizing energy output. This study offers valuable insights for policymakers and stakeholders, showcasing aquavoltaics as a scalable framework for balancing food production, renewable energy generation, and climate adaptation—advancing sustainable aquaculture in Taiwan and beyond.

title: Pre-optimization-based deep reinforcement learning for autonomous economic and exergy management of stochastic H2/CO ratio syngas switching downstream processes
abstract: Driven by global warming and escalating energy demand, sustainable syngas production continues to advance as an essential cleaner energy carrier. The switching of the syngas H2/CO ratio can supply tailored feedstock for synthesizing diverse downstream chemicals. However, unsteady state, stochastic behavior, and plant-model mismatch characteristics of the downstream process complicate existing control strategies and operational management. This study addresses the critical challenge of intelligent operational management in stochastic syngas switching downstream (SSSD) processes characterized by strong stochasticity and dynamic losses. To this end, a pre-optimization-based deep reinforcement learning (DRL) control framework is proposed for autonomous economic and exergy (2E) management of SSSD process. First, a high-fidelity dynamic model of SSSD process is developed to simulate the stochastic behavior and dynamic losses of the system. Then, the optimization constraint algorithm is innovatively embedded into the DRL framework to obtain an optimized initial set of actions for each random reset. Finally, the agent is trained to interact with the dynamic model in pursuit of efficient exploration and reward, which produces an optimal control strategy. The proposed method reduces exergy destruction by 3.8 % and 2.1 % compared to proportional-integral-derivative (PID) and conventional DRL frameworks, while obtaining the minimum operating cost of $8542 and the most stable product control. The well-trained agent is also able to self-adapt to process uncertainties with higher exploration efficiency and stability, achieving intelligent and sustainable production for complex and dynamic processes.

title: Energy-integrated plastic-to-X optimization via machine learning-embedded graph-theoretic approach: EU 27 study
abstract: The growing environmental and economic challenges associated with plastic waste call for sustainable recycling solutions that align with circular economy principles and energy decarbonization goals. This work develops a novel machine learning-embedded multi-objective graph-theoretic (P-graph) optimization framework to evaluate plastic-to-X pathways across the EU-27, also considering Norway. Four recycling strategies are examined: mechanical recycling (plastic-to-plastic), pyrolysis to pyro-oil (plastic-to-fuel), gasification to methanol (plastic-to-chemical), and incineration (plastic-to-energy), each applied to four plastic compositions, i.e., mixed plastics (MP), polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polystyrene (PS). The model integrates country-specific electricity mixes and normalizes performance based on both net total cost and CO 2 emissions using surrogate models derived from process simulations and literature data. Results show that pathway selection is influenced by both plastic composition and the national electricity profile. Mechanical recycling is economically favored for pure streams like PE, while pyrolysis dominates PS and PP due to high oil yields and low emissions. For MP, a hybrid approach combining mechanical recycling and methanol production is consistently selected. This work shows that cleaner energy mixes provide more options for plastic-to-X pathways when aiming to minimize costs and environmental impact at similar treatment potential. Further analysis of the top 1000 near-optimal solutions reveals that combining multiple pathways is attractive as opposed to single technologies. Overall, this work provides an ex-ante decision support framework for optimizing plastic waste valorization under region specific energy conditions.

title: Multi-step battery temperature prediction for electric vehicles: Vehicle identification-driven long short-term memory neural networks based on real-world charging pile data
abstract: Accurate prediction of battery temperature is critical for ensuring the safety of electric vehicles (EVs), which are pivotal for achieving cleaner transportation and reduced carbon emissions. Current research on battery temperature prediction relies primarily on laboratory or onboard battery management systems (BMS) data. However, these data sources have limitations in reflecting the complexity of real-world charging scenarios. In addition, the lack of vehicle identification information in charging pile data challenges accurate temperature prediction. To address this issue, this paper proposes a new approach that combines vehicle identification and grouping with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to predict battery temperature using real-world charging pile data. This study first proposes a multi-parameter disparity-based vehicle identification grouping (MPDVIG) strategy to group the charging data by vehicle identification. Then, the LSTM model is used to predict the temperature based on the overall and grouped data. By comparing the results of the two approaches, it is found that the accuracy of the method of identification followed by prediction is higher. For instance, the mean relative error for the highest temperature predictions decreased from 1.45 % to 1.06 %. This is the first time the LSTM model has been applied to the battery temperature prediction based on the real-world charging pile data, providing a reference for the subsequent safety warning.

title: Machine learning-optimized efficient CO2-to-CO conversion in a novel catalyst-free spark discharge plasma
abstract: Catalyst-free spark-discharge plasma offers a promising new route for CO2 utilization via the reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction, yet strong coupling among power, residence time, composition, and reactor geometry complicates deployment-relevant optimization. An improved coaxial quartz-tube spark-discharge reactor is considered, and a structured dataset of 500 operating points is compiled by varying discharge power, total flow rate, H2/CO2 molar ratio, and inner-tube diameter across engineering-relevant levels. To avoid inflated generalization caused by random splits on grid-like datasets, ten regressors are screened using leave-one-condition-out grouped cross-validation, and an artificial neural network (ANN; multilayer perceptron, MLP) surrogate is selected and tuned under the strict leave-one-diameter-out protocol with early stopping. Hyperparameter tuning improves grouped predictive accuracy to R2 = 0.909 for CO2 conversion and R2 = 0.970 for energy efficiency. Model credibility is further supported by bootstrap resampling, applicability-domain diagnostics, and external interpolation validation on 15 off-grid points (R2 = 0.907 for conversion and 0.959 for efficiency), with most observations captured within the 95 % prediction band. Operating-window maps identify a peak conversion of 89.76 % at 70 W, H2/CO2 = 3.0, 200 mL/min and an inner-tube diameter of 7 mm, and a peak energy efficiency of 19.12 % at 40 W, H2/CO2 = 1.0, 1000 mL/min and 7 mm, under bench-scale laboratory conditions. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) interpretation provides process-relevant attribution of nonlinear effects and clarifies interaction-driven regime dependence within the validated domain. The resulting workflow enables specification-driven, electricity-aware screening to finalize reactor configuration and operating windows for downstream syngas applications.

title: Explainable machine learning and life cycle assessment for sustainable design of fiber-reinforced asphalt concrete
abstract: Conventional asphalt concrete has a limited lifespan due to cracking, deformation, and environmental degradation, driving the development of fiber-reinforced asphalt concrete (FRAC). However, key gaps remain in current data-driven FRAC studies due to small and homogeneous datasets, “black-box” machine learning models, and trade-offs between mechanical-sustainable performance, failing to provide a transparent understanding of features governing FRAC behaviors. This paper proposes a framework integrating explainable artificial intelligence and life cycle assessment (LCA) to advance mechanical and sustainable design of FRAC. A dataset of 2490 laboratory samples covers 15 input features and 3 mechanical outputs. Eight machine learning models, along with a voting ensemble strategy, were optimized using Genetic algorithm for hyperparameter tuning. The optimized voting ensemble achieved an average prediction performance of R 2 = 0.87, RMSE = 1.09, MAPE = 11.96%, and MAE = 0.60 across the three mechanical targets, indicating robust and reliable predictive capability. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis and linear non-gaussian acyclic causal inference quantified global/local feature impacts and pairwise interactions. LCA evaluated economic and environmental impacts and derived strength-normalized sustainability metrics. Finally, an interactive graphic user interface platform was developed for predictions, SHAP interpretations, and LCA outcomes. This data-driven approach establishes a paradigm for intelligent FRAC design, harmonizing mechanical performance with sustainability. • A dataset of 2490 laboratory samples was constructed for fiber-reinforced asphalt concrete. • The dataset comprises 15 design parameters as inputs and 3 mechanical properties as outputs. • 9 machine learning models were optimized using genetic algorithm for hyperparameter tuning. • The SHAP algorithm and causal inference were used to interpret optimal predictions. • A life cycle assessment was conducted to evaluate cost, carbon footprint, and energy efficiency.

title: Attribution analysis of spatial differentiation in green and low-carbon transition and development efficiency based on geographical detector and random forest models: A case study of the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Green and low-carbon transition and development represents a global issue encompassing economic, social and environmental dimensions. To objectively assess the efficiency of this transition, this study establishes an evaluation index system from input-output perspectives of economy, resources and society, focusing on 108 prefecture-level cities along the Yangtze River Economic Belt. Through trend surface analysis and spatial autocorrelation methods, we investigate the spatio-temporal characteristics of green and low-carbon transition and development efficiency during 2011–2022. The geographical detector method integrated with random forest model is employed to identify driving factors. The main result are as follows: (1) Distinct spatial disparities in transition efficiency across the economic belt, with an overall upward trend despite suboptimal efficiency levels. Regional clusters demonstrate intensified agglomeration patterns, exhibiting a “high-east-west, low-central” spatial configuration. (2) Spatial positive correlations show increasing trends, with local spatial clusters predominantly manifesting as high-high or low-low agglomerations. (3) Dynamic variations in factor explanatory power across study years, with enhanced combined effects through factor interactions. Notably, the top three determinants, industrial development level, urban development level, and social consumption level exhibit nonlinear relationships with transition efficiency, while the nature of these relationships varies. This research provides empirical evidence for understanding regional transition mechanisms and offers decision-making support for formulating differentiated green development strategies.

title: Federated reinforcement learning-based dynamic hosting domain for electric vehicles charging management in distribution networks with renewable energy resources
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources and electric vehicles (EVs) introduces considerable uncertainty into distribution networks, where renewable intermittency and uncoordinated charging can cause voltage violations, congestion, and reduced hosting capability. Conventional static assessment methods, based on fixed operating assumptions, fail to capture the spatiotemporal interactions induced by renewable variability and aggregated charging demand under network constraints. To address these challenges, this study proposes a dynamic hosting domain (DHD) framework based on reinforcement learning. The DHD defines the time-varying feasible region of system states, providing a quantitative representation of admissible operating boundaries with explicit physical safety guarantees. It adapts to spatiotemporal charging variations and incorporates a margin-based index for hosting capacity evaluation. A station-level delay perception model is embedded into the reward design to account for aggregated service-quality constraints as macroscopic economic feedback, discouraging excessive charging postponement while preserving operational feasibility at the system level. Furthermore, a federated reinforcement learning architecture based on proximal policy optimization (PPO) enables collaborative policy learning among multiple charging stations without raw data sharing, thereby enhancing scalability, privacy preservation, and spatiotemporal coordination under non-IID conditions. Case studies on renewable-integrated distribution networks demonstrate faster convergence, enhanced voltage stability, and lower operational costs compared with benchmarks. The proposed DHD framework offers a unified pathway for secure, efficient, and behavior-aware EV charging management in renewable-energy-integrated systems.

title: A mechanistic machine learning framework to decode reverse osmosis membrane retention mechanism for neutral low-molecular-weight organics
abstract: Neutral low-molecular-weight (LMW) organics (e.g., urea, N-nitrosodimethylamine) with molecular weights <250 Da can permeate reverse osmosis (RO) membranes, compromising reclaimed water quality and posing health and industrial risks. However, the permeation characteristics of LMW organics and the mechanisms governing their retention are unclear. This study innovatively integrated data-driven machine learning (ML) with physicochemical mechanisms to decode RO retention characteristics and mechanisms of neutral LMW organics. A comprehensive database of 1254 retention data points for 190 organics was built, and six ML algorithms were evaluated. The XGBoost model, optimized via physicochemical mechanism-guided feature engineering (capturing steric, van der Waals, electrostatic, and hydrophobic interactions), achieved an adjusted R2 of 0.91 and MAE of 3.53%, outperforming traditional models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed steric and van der Waals effects as core retention mechanisms, with cross-mechanism synergies between steric and van der Waals interactions dominating retention. This framework mitigated data leakage (MAE reduced from 15.78% to 2.76% via compound-based splitting) and guided membrane design strategies: tuning pore size <0.4 nm for steric exclusion, enhancing polarizability for van der Waals adsorption, and optimizing pH-responsive charge layers. The study provided a transformative engineering roadmap for next-generation RO membranes, bridging data-driven predictions with mechanistic material design for sustainable water management.

title: Research on remote sensing ecological index prediction based on deep learning—Taking the application of long short-term memory neural network in Yili prefecture as an example
abstract: Ecological monitoring is often limited by the lag in post-event assessment, while predicting future ecological conditions is crucial for proactive environmental management. Therefore, we developed a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to predict the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) for the study area in 2025 and employed the Shapley Additive Interpretation (SHAP) method to explain the relative contributions of natural and anthropogenic factors. Studies show that drastic land-use change reduces prediction accuracy; therefore, we introduced a regional correction mechanism based on Bayesian conjugate priors to integrate land-use information into the deep learning prediction. This method was applied to the Ili region of Xinjiang, China, and performed well compared to measured data from 2020. Furthermore, its predicted regional average index for 2025 is consistent with the persistence indicated by the Hurst index. The study shows that ecological foundation and precipitation are the main positive drivers of future ecological quality, while high temperatures, soil drought, and intensive urbanization and grazing activities will reduce ecological quality. The results of the global bivariate Moran's index indicate a spatial correlation between land use change intensity and model residuals; areas with greater change are more likely to be adjacent to areas with larger prediction biases. Furthermore, we introduced a confidence parameter to measure the relative confidence between prior and predicted values and determined the optimal setting for balancing goodness of fit and robustness. Our research not only improves the model's predictive accuracy in areas of rapid land use transition, but also integrates spatial planning with ecological prediction. The findings support policymakers in anticipating multiple possible ecological outcomes when developing different regional planning pathways.

title: Climate dynamics and air quality interactions: Machine learning analysis of diurnal temperature range drivers in three major Bangladesh cities
abstract: Satellite-derived land surface temperature diurnal range (LST-DTR), computed as the difference between MODIS daytime and nighttime LST, acts as a meaningful proxy for surface radiative dynamics in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study employed three machine learning algorithms (Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, and Decision Tree) integrated with SHAP importance analysis to quantify the impacts of black carbon (BC), PM2.5, aerosol, and albedo on LST-DTR across three major Bangladesh cities: Dhaka, Chattogram, and Rajshahi. Satellite-derived MODIS and MERRA-2 data (2001-2023) were analyzed using 5-fold cross-validation, yielding moderate yet stable model performance (R2 = 0.35-0.43; RMSE = 2.04-2.51). SHAP analysis showed BC as the dominant predictor in all three cities (SHAP importance: 0.94-1.59), highlighting its key role in urban land surface thermal dynamics through radiative absorption and surface albedo modification. Albedo emerged as a key secondary factor (0.30–1.27), ranking highest in Rajshahi, where it nearly matched BC, while Aerosols ranked second in Dhaka and Chattogram (0.27–0.94), and PM2.5 had the weakest influence (0.08-0.35). The dominance of BC over PM2.5 in LST-DTR modulation suggests that current air quality policies, which primarily focus on particulate matter, may overlook the most critical driver of urban land-surface thermal variability. The study provides evidence for targeted actions: encouraging diesel particulate filters, updating kiln technology, urban greening with high-albedo vegetation in fast-growing zones, and cool roofing with reflective materials. These findings inform evidence-based environmental policies for sustainable urban development in rapidly expanding South Asian cities.

title: Longterm dynamics of plastisphere succession and polymer degradation mechanisms in marine environments: A 12-month in-situ study with machine learning applications
abstract: The escalating global crisis of marine plastic pollution underscores the urgent need to investigate longterm weathering mechanisms and associated ecological risks under environmental conditions. In this study, a 12-month in-situ exposure experiment was conducted in a subtropical marine environment to systematically elucidate the degradation dynamics of polypropylene (PP) and polylactic acid (PLA) and their interactions with microbial communities. Results demonstrate polymer-specific aging patterns and biofilm-enhanced risks, revealing that cyanobacteria (harmful algal bloom initiators) preferentially colonize persistent PP (12–15% abundance) over biodegradable PLA (0.22–0.26%). The persistence of PP in the environment enables stable cyanobacterial biofilms to act as longterm dispersal vectors for algal bloom initiation. In contrast, PLA surfaces were enriched with hydrolytic bacteria (e.g., Firmicutes), and this colonization was associated with enhanced mass loss and secondary microplastic formation. Furthermore, seasonal variations exerted limited control over dominant plastisphere taxa, with microbial communities on homogeneous plastics converging over time. Polymer type dominated plastisphere assembly, followed by exposure duration and physical form. Moreover, a deep convolutional neural network (CNN)-based machine learning (ML) model was developed to predict the weathering degree of plastics, achieving a highly reliable accuracy of 85.3 ± 0.8% by extracting image features of the weathered plastic surface, offering a novel paradigm for longterm ecological risk assessment. This work indicates that the short-term experiments are insufficient for predicting the fate of plastics and highlights the necessity of integrating multimodal data into extended observational frameworks and direct measures of microbial activity to evaluate ecological risks more accurately.

title: Linking land cover changes to carbon storage in Hunan Province, China: Insights from multi-task learning
abstract: Long-term land cover dynamics are a key regulator of regional carbon storage, yet most assessments still rely on a few temporal snapshots and therefore overlook how land transitions unfold over time. Here we reconstruct annual land cover in Hunan Province, China, from 1990 to 2023 using a multi-task deep learning framework, and combine it with climate-corrected carbon accounting, driver attribution and future scenario simulation. Although total carbon storage increased from 2122.74 Mt in 1990 to 2209.98 Mt in 2023 in Hunan, this net gain masked pronounced spatial heterogeneity and distinct carbon responses to land cover transition frequency and pathways. Trajectory analysis further showed that different change frequencies and transition pathways produced distinct carbon consequences, with return-type pathways tending toward near-neutral responses and directional pathways leading to clearer carbon gains or losses. The dominant drivers of carbon storage were also not stationary, with vegetation condition prevailing in 2000 and 2020, whereas population density became most important in 2010. Interactions among vegetation condition, topography, and population density mainly shaped spatial heterogeneity in carbon storage. Historical-trend simulation further indicates that regional carbon storage growth may decelerate sharply by 2030, with only a marginal increase of 1.35 Mt relative to 2020. These findings are particularly concerning because the potential to offset the carbon costs of continued urban expansion through land conversion alone may be increasingly limited, making the protection of existing high-carbon ecological spaces more urgent.

title: Corporate-level climate risk prediction: A comparative machine learning framework
abstract: Accurately predicting corporate climate risk is critical for climate-sensitive finance and policy. Using a panel of China's A-share listed firms (2004–2023), this study constructs a forward-looking, firm-specific climate-risk indicator via textual analysis of annual reports and integrates a comprehensive set of predictors that capture both internal firm characteristics and external climate-environmental exposure. Predictions are evaluated within a rigorous expanding-window out-of-sample framework that strictly prevents look-ahead bias. Systematic comparison of a broad spectrum of models—from classical econometric baselines to traditional machine learning and deep learning—reveals that advanced machine learning models collectively achieve an average out-of-sample R2 of 0.601, a 304.6% improvement over traditional baselines (average R2 = 0.149). Deep-learning architectures, especially Attention-LSTM (R2 = 0.815), LSTM, and CNN, deliver the highest predictive accuracy by capturing complex long-term temporal dependencies. Gradient-boosting trees (LightGBM, CatBoost) provide the best trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency, whereas ensemble methods such as Stacking show robustness at higher computational cost. SHAP-based interpretability analysis of the best-performing models identifies debt investments the most influential predictor, with higher levels consistently associated with elevated climate-risk forecasts. Critically, externally measured climate variables—provincial physical-risk indices and city-level climate-policy uncertainty—rank among the top predictors, confirming that objective climate exposure and policy volatility are fundamental to the model's risk assessment. A counter-intuitive yet robust pattern is the positive contribution of green-patent counts, suggesting that firms facing strong transition pressure may be simultaneously active in green innovation. Interaction analysis further reveals that the marginal effect of debt investment is highly context-dependent, varying with internal firm attributes (age, asset structure, size) and external conditions (industry concentration, physical risk, institutional quality). This underscores that climate-risk formation is a non-linear outcome of coupled financial, organizational, and environmental factors. The study demonstrates the substantial predictive gain offered by machine learning, provides a granular mapping of algorithmic performance, and unveils the multidimensional, interactive statistical associations that drive climate-risk forecasts. These findings offer both methodological and empirical foundations for more resilient risk-management infrastructure and climate-informed decision-making.

title: Reinforcement learning control of pilot-scale solvent recovery for battery manufacturing: Surrogate-assisted optimization with techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment
abstract: As electric-vehicle battery manufacturing scales up, its environmental footprint grows, primarily driven by the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from using N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone in electrode fabrication. Establishing an efficient closed-loop recycling process for this solvent is therefore essential to advance a circular economy and align with emerging eco-design principles. To systematically minimize the GHG emissions of battery manufacturing, this study presents a surrogate-assisted reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the solvent recycling process, validated with data from a pilot-scale plant. The framework integrates a first-principles dynamic model developed in Aspen Plus Dynamics, a physics-constrained neural ordinary differential equation surrogate model, and an RL agent to jointly optimize reflux-ratio trajectories and batch termination under a stringent purity requirement of 99.99 wt%. Techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment modules translate control policies into quantitative production cost and GHG outcomes. As a result, the recycling process achieves GHG emissions of 0.222 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilogram of recovered solvent, compared to 8.06 kilograms for virgin production. Furthermore, the learned RL policies reduce production cost by up to 3.8% and decrease GHG emissions by up to 57%, relative to the worst-case fixed reflux ratio scenario. This pilot-validated framework provides a scalable pathway toward sustainable solvent-recovery practice in battery manufacturing, demonstrating that RL-based control can deliver both operational feasibility and environmental benefits.

title: Deciphering the multivariable interactions of MOFs in heavy metal adsorption via explainable machine learning for sustainable and resource-efficient adsorbent development
abstract: Heavy metals (HMs) in aquatic environments seriously threaten ecosystems and human health. Although metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have shown great potential for HMs removal, adsorption performance is governed by complex interactions between material characteristics and operating conditions. However, while existing studies largely emphasize performance prediction, systematic data-driven frameworks for decoding these interactions and guiding adsorbent design remain limited. This study constructed a comprehensive dataset comprising 4289 samples, incorporating MOF characteristics, experimental conditions, and adsorption data for Cr(VI), Pb(II), Cd(II), and As(V). Large-scale data mining was performed using explainable machine learning. Key findings include: the solution volume and shaker speed must be systematically investigated as critical parameters to enable a clear mechanistic discussion of the adsorption material and reliable performance comparison. The strong synergistic or antagonistic relationships between MOF components and experimental conditions were systematically explained as decisive for adsorption behaviors, highlighting the necessity of integrated parameter optimization for efficient adsorbent development and process design. The initial concentration of pollutants and reaction time showed significant interactive effects with other factors. In contrast, 95% of feature importance results consistently indicate that organic ligands exert a stronger influence on adsorption capacity, while coordination metals more readily affect removal rate. Finally, eight representative MOF compositions were identified for different environmental scenarios. This work establishes an explainable, data-driven decision-support framework that transforms adsorption data into actionable design knowledge, supporting resource-efficient material development and sustainable environmental remediation.

title: Scaling sustainable protein production: Integrating farmer knowledge with AI to optimize black soldier fly larvae cultivation
abstract: The transition toward a circular bio-economy requires scalable technologies for organic waste upcycling and sustainable protein production. Black Soldier Fly (BSF) farming has emerged as a promising approach for waste-to-resource conversion; however, its industrial expansion is constrained by biological variability and the lack of robust optimization tools suitable for decentralized production systems. This study presents a farmer-partnered Decision Support System (DSS) that applies machine learning to optimize larval biomass yield and nutritional quality, including protein and fat content, using real-world data collected across multiple farms. The proposed DSS follows a data-centric approach that integrates practitioner domain expertise with longitudinal experimental data while accounting for the biological variability inherent in organic side-streams. We evaluate cross-farm generalization compared to personalized modeling strategies and analyze how shared datasets can improve prediction reliability in heterogeneous farming environments. To support practical adoption, the system incorporates explainability and interactive visualizations that enable farmers to better understand how diet composition influences larval growth and nutrient outcomes. The results demonstrate that integrating data science with farmer knowledge can improve process consistency and resource efficiency in BSF production systems, contributing to reduced reliance on marine-derived feed inputs and supporting progress toward UN Sustainable Development Goals related to responsible production and environmental sustainability.

title: A process-informed framework for deriving groundwater-protective soil thresholds for PPCPs by integrating machine learning and vadose-zone transport modeling
abstract: Conventional approaches for deriving groundwater-protective soil thresholds for pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) often simplify subsurface transport and neglect attenuation in the vadose zone, which can lead to overly conservative screening outcomes. To support more realistic and proportionate groundwater protection, this study developed a process-informed framework that integrates machine learning with HYDRUS-based vadose zone transport modeling. A global dataset covering 24 PPCPs and 584 soil and sediment samples was first used to predict the solid–liquid partition coefficient (Kd), and the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) model showed the best performance. The results indicated that molecular properties and soil organic carbon were the major controls on partitioning. Vadose zone attenuation factors (AF) were then quantified by coupling HYDRUS simulations with machine learning, and the best performing model achieved an R2 of 0.90. Depth, KOC, and precipitation were identified as the dominant controls on attenuation, accounting for 76% of the total contribution. By integrating Kd, AF, and groundwater dilution factor (DF), groundwater-protective soil thresholds were derived for trimethoprim, nalidixic acid, and niflumic acid, with HC5 values of 0.06, 0.80, and 41.12 mg kg−1, respectively. Compared with conventional EPA-style calculations, explicitly accounting for vadose-zone attenuation materially changed the threshold estimates. These findings demonstrate that explicit representation of vadose-zone processes improves the realism of soil screening and supports science-based site management and groundwater risk control for emerging contaminants.

title: A hybrid machine learning framework for enhanced day-ahead solar forecasting in large scale systems
abstract: Accurate solar power forecasting is becoming increasingly crucial for the efficient planning and operation of modern power systems as solar energy constitutes a growing share of the energy mix. This work evaluates the performance of various artificial neural network (ANN) models for day-ahead solar power forecasting. Through two case studies, it examines the impact of seasonal and weather-related variations on large-scale distributed solar generation. The analysis draws on solar power generation and weather data from the Imperial Irrigation District (IID) and the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) in the United States from January 2019 to December 2022, with over 20,000 h of operational data. The bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) model demonstrated the highest accuracy in day-ahead solar power forecasting and was selected as the baseline for comparison. To further improve prediction accuracy, two ensemble approaches, namely weighted averaging and multi-input, were explored. The results show that both approaches improve forecasting performance relative to the baseline, yielding positive MAE-based skill score improvements on the order of several percent across seasons. In particular, weighted averaging provides stronger and more consistent gains in the IID case study, with skill score improvements reaching approximately 11% in favorable seasons, whereas the multi-input ensemble demonstrates more consistently favorable performance in the LADWP case study, achieving skill score improvements of up to about 13%. These findings suggest that ensemble formulations provide a practical framework for improving day-ahead solar power forecasting in large-scale distributed PV systems. The results further indicate that performance depends on regional characteristics and the structure of available meteorological inputs.

title: Navigating the global expanse of offshore floating photovoltaics: Techno-ecological-economic boundaries decoded by artificial intelligence
abstract: Offshore floating photovoltaics (OFPV) offer a massive frontier for global clean energy without land competition, yet theoretical estimates ignore severe marine limitations and risks. This paper, for the first time, proposes a novel “virtual expert” framework to capture the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of marine environments for data-driven suitability assessment of global OFPV potential. Under current-stage assumptions, our analysis reveals that within Exclusive Economic Zones, stringent techno-environmental constraints curtail the initial 14,831,550 TWh/year (128.94 million km2) theoretical potential by 93.7%. This yields a realizable potential of 935,110 TWh/year across 9.04 million km2, underscoring the profound impact of technical and environmental thresholds on OFPV expansion. Regionally, Asia dominates in absolute potential, while Africa boasts the highest average suitability, with specific cyclone-exempt African nations achieving 100% “most suitable” coverage as promising early-stage deployment candidates. Constraint analysis identifies water depth as the primary physical barrier, eliminating vast high-radiance areas across Europe, the Americas, and Africa. Meanwhile, sea ice and marine protected areas impose absolute exclusions in high-latitude and ecological hotspots, whereas low-latitude deployments—notably in Asia and Oceania—demand robust tropical cyclone resilience. Furthermore, spatially resolved techno-economic assessments reveal that while unconstrained marine areas achieve an average levelized cost of energy of 9.16 US cents/kWh under standardized economic assumptions, some constrained zones nevertheless retain relatively favorable solar economics, suggesting that deep-water station-keeping and cyclone-resilient floating structures may become high-priority R&D directions for future OFPV innovation. Ultimately, these findings demonstrate that OFPV deployment is inherently a highly localized spatial optimization challenge, our framework providing a macro-siting tool to assist stakeholders in balancing clean energy expansion with marine conservation and environmental risk mitigation.

title: Interpretable machine learning reveals multi-scale controls on groundwater fluoride across the Shanxi rift system
abstract: Groundwater fluoride in the Shanxi Rift System displays marked spatial heterogeneity, with high-fluoride basins occurring adjacent to zones of totally low concentrations. This study investigates the factors responsible for this contrast by applying an interpretable machine-learning framework that integrates supervised model comparison with posterior interpretation analyses. The modelling reveals a distinct scale dependence in fluoride controls. At the basin scale, fluoride enrichment is primarily influenced by hydrochemical conditions dominated by Ca2+ and HCO3−. At the cross-basin scale, however, the dominant control shifts to geological setting, particularly the distance to carbonate formations. Short distances correspond to higher Ca2+ and lower HCO3− conditions, resulting in hydrochemical “non-responsive intervals” in which fluoride concentrations remain low and insensitive to further changes in Ca2+ and HCO3−. This mechanism accounts for the anomalously low fluoride levels observed in the Changzhi Basin. Overall, the results demonstrate that fluoride distribution in the Shanxi Rift System is shaped by the combined effects of local hydrochemical equilibria and regional geological structure, and highlight the importance of explicitly considering spatial scale when interpreting the processes governing geogenic fluoride contamination.

title: On track but too slow? The dynamics of EU decarbonization
abstract: Despite the strong commitment of European countries to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, the extent to which key policies and drivers jointly shape emissions dynamics remains insufficiently investigated. The study suggests that the interaction among circular economy, energy transition, emissions trading systems, carbon tax, and digitalization policies creates structural constraints on CO 2 emissions in the European countries. Using annual data from 2000 to 2023, the analysis integrates exploratory causal discovery, time-varying dependence modeling, and machine learning methods to unravel system-level causal structure, dynamic connectedness, and future emission trajectories. The results indicate that resource productivity emerges as a central transmission channel within the system, linking upstream factors (material footprint) and digitalization to downstream emission outcomes. Lagged disequilibrium shocks propagate through resource use as a mediating channel. Time-varying copula models indicate significant heterogeneity and evolving dependence among key factors, highlighting the dynamic nature of policy and relationships over time. Forecasting results, based on a Support Vector Regression model under the European Union's 2030 climate policy framework, indicate a persistently declining emission trajectory, but at a pace insufficient to meet the EU's 2030 target. Sensitivity analysis suggests that this gap does not primarily reflect a policy failure, but the structural limitations in how policy interactions translate into decarbonization outcomes. These findings highlight the need to improve the effectiveness of policy instruments by strengthening resource productivity and accelerating progress toward the targets.

title: Auto-optimized interpretable machine learning for terminal water quality prediction of the ultrapure water production system in the semiconductor industry: demonstration in a full-scale system
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, maintaining ultrapure water (UPW) quality at the terminal is critical for product safety. However, early prediction and warning of water quality deterioration remain challenging due to complex process interactions and limited monitoring responsiveness. This study developed interpretable machine learning models for 1-h-ahead prediction of terminal total organic carbon (TOC) and resistivity in a full-scale UPW system (48 m3/d). Six modeling approaches were evaluated, and XGBoost and Random Forest (RF) were selected as the optimal models for TOC and resistivity prediction, respectively. After hyperparameter optimization, the Optuna-XGBoost model achieved an R2 of 0.9664 for TOC prediction, while the RS-RF model achieved an R2 of 0.9670 for resistivity prediction. Model interpretation using SHAP and partial dependence analysis identified return water resistivity as a key influencing factor for both targets, suggesting that return water may act as a potential risk source. Strong nonlinear interaction effects were observed, particularly between first- and second-stage RO rejection rates for TOC prediction, and between return water resistivity and first-stage RO rejection for resistivity prediction. In addition, models were developed for RO membrane rejection rates. First-stage rejection was mainly governed by historical behavior, whereas second-stage rejection depended on influent conductivity and operational conditions. The proposed framework enables reliable 1-h-ahead prediction and early warning of water quality deterioration, supporting proactive operational strategies such as return water management and RO/VUV/mixed bed optimization. Overall, this work demonstrates the value of interpretable auto machine learning for early warning and decision support in semiconductor UPW systems.

title: Uncovering the burden shifting of data center cooling: System-level water-energy-carbon optimization for urban infrastructure
abstract: The rapid growth of data centers (DCs), driven by artificial intelligence and cloud computing, presents a critical resource challenge for urban infrastructure planning across the water-energy-carbon nexus. Traditional energy models often treat DC integration merely as an isolated electrical load, failing to capture weather-dependent cooling demands and the resulting "burden-shifting" between direct on-site water consumption and the indirect water footprint of the regional grid. To bridge this gap, this study introduces a multi-scale mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) optimization framework for urban capacity expansion planning that explicitly integrates hourly climate data with the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) of distinct DC cooling architectures. Applied to a representative urban microgrid, the model simulates a multi-year horizon at an hourly resolution to evaluate two contrasting DC cooling strategies: evaporative cooling and closed-loop air chillers. Our results reveal a critical trade-off: optimizing exclusively for zero on-site water use via air chillers inadvertently shifts the resource burden upstream to the regional electrical grid, demanding substantial increases in low-carbon generation, energy storage, and total infrastructure costs. Ultimately, moving beyond facility-specific metrics to evaluate holistic, system-wide Pareto trade-offs is essential for developing sustainable urban energy strategies.

title: An integrated machine learning and MATLAB/Simulink framework for enhanced photovoltaic power forecasting and grid integration
abstract: The rapid integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into modern power grids requires energy forecasting approaches that are both statistically accurate and physically consistent. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that combines machine–learning–based prediction with physics-based validation in MATLAB/Simulink. The key contribution is a two-layer validation workflow in which data-driven ensemble forecasts are evaluated against a grid-connected PV simulation model to assess their physical feasibility under realistic operating conditions. The proposed framework employs a stacking ensemble that integrates complementary tree-based and neural-network-based learners and is evaluated across multiple datasets, including reanalysis-based meteorological data and field-measured PV outputs. Results show that the stacking ensemble achieves an RMSE of 0.022, MAE of 0.011, and R2 of 0.996 on the reanalysis-based dataset (MERRA-2). On real-world (Northern Hemisphere) PV data, the model achieves an RMSE of 4.7211 W, MAE of 3.5061 W, and R2 of 0.5612, while independent meteorological data (NSRDB) yield an RMSE of 0.0554 W, MAE of 0.0297 W, and R2 of 0.9815, demonstrating competitive performance across different operating conditions. Statistical comparisons indicate that the ensemble achieves significant improvements in MAE relative to benchmark models in selected datasets while remaining competitive on RMSE. To enhance interpretability, LIME-based analysis is used to quantify the influence of meteorological features, and ablation studies are conducted to assess the contribution and robustness of the ensemble architecture. Physics-based validation using a 10-kW grid-connected Simulink model demonstrates that the predicted power trajectories are consistent with converter dynamics and operational constraints, with an average deviation of approximately 3% and an RMSE of 0.182 kW between the machine-learning predictions and simulation outputs. Additional validation using reanalysis data from Tamil Nadu indicates promising generalization, although evaluation remains limited to specific sites and conditions. Long-term forecasting that incorporates degradation effects is also explored to extend the framework for planning applications. Overall, the proposed approach provides a structured pathway for integrating data-driven forecasting with engineering validation, enabling more reliable renewable energy integration, improved energy management, and resource-efficient grid operations that support the transition toward cleaner electricity production.

title: Machine learning-based integration of plant growth regulators and overcompensation enhances microalgal protein production from wastewater
abstract: Photoautotrophic wastewater valorization represents a sustainable route for carbon-neutral nutrient upcycling into bioproducts. However, its practical implementation is often constrained by wastewater-induced growth inhibition. Besides, the distribution of metabolic flux across competing pathways may further restrict nutrient allocation towards target product. In this study, we propose a combined strategy integrating plant growth regulators (PGRs) with a nitrogen overcompensation strategy to enhance microalgal performance during potato starch wastewater treatment. Gibberellic acid (GA 3 ) and naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA) both alleviated wastewater inhibition and enhanced nutrient recovery in Chlorella pyrenoidosa , achieving up to 79.9% total nitrogen removal. Notably, supplementation with 10 mg L −1 GA 3 resulted in a 26.2% increase in biomass compared to controls. The random forest model identified candidate high-response concentrations of approximately 10.5 ± 1 mg L −1 for GA 3 and 10.2 ± 1 mg L −1 for NAA and suggested declining biomass responses at higher NAA concentrations, whereas GA 3 showed a broader model-predicted growth-promoting range. Under the nitrogen starvation–repletion condition, PGR-supplemented cultures achieved maximum biomass and protein concentrations of up to 1.58 g L −1 and 594.82 mg L −1 , respectively, together with over 90% removal of COD, total phosphorus, and ammonium. Transcriptomic profiling indicated that GA 3 induced significant upregulation of genes involved in photosynthetic apparatus function, ribosomal biogenesis, and transmembrane transport processes compared to NAA. This work establishes a strategy that integrates PGRs with nitrogen overcompensation to overcome wastewater-induced stress. The proposed approach provides a practical strategy for improving microalgal productivity and nutrient recovery from high-strength wastewater, advancing the development of carbon-neutral biorefinery systems.

title: Interpretable machine learning insights into the impact of environmental regulation on low-carbon transition: Evidence from the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Environmental regulation (ER) has become an important instrument for achieving environmental goals and advancing the low-carbon transition (LCT). However, existing studies still suffer from several limitations, including incomplete indicator systems, difficulties in capturing the nonlinear relationship and multifactor interaction effects between ER and LCT, and a lack of empirical analyses at the watershed scale. Consequently, the mechanism through which ER affects LCT warrants further in-depth exploration. To address these gaps, this study employs panel data from 108 cities in the Yangtze River Economic Belt from 2010 to 2023 to reveal the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics of ER and LCT and applies the XGBoost-SHAP model to identify the impact of ER on LCT. The results show that: (1) the spatial patterns of both ER and LCT present high values in the east and low values in the west, with high-value areas gradually agglomerating toward core regions, such as the Yangtze River Delta; (2) ER contributes 20.87% to LCT and exhibits a significant threshold effect, with its positive impact increasing markedly when ER exceeds 0.338; (3) synergistic effects between ER and factors such as urban transportation and financial development significantly enhance LCT. This study constructed a multidimensional evaluation system for ER and LCT and, for the first time, revealed the nonlinear threshold mechanism and multifactor synergy rules of ER affecting LCT at the watershed scale of the Yangtze River Economic Belt. This provides new empirical evidence for understanding their interaction mechanism and offers implications for optimizing the LCT pathways in this region.

title: Attributing streamflow extremes under compound scenarios via hybrid of explainable AI and hydrological modeling: Implications for sustainable watershed management
abstract: Accurate projection and attribution of streamflow extremes under compound climate and climate and land-use scenarios are critical for sustainable watershed management, yet conventional assessments predominantly evaluate isolated factors and overlook dynamic anthropogenic regulations. This study develops an integrated scenario-based hybrid attribution analysis of streamflow extremes (abbreviated as SHASE) framework for (i) tackling non-linear boundary inflows and reservoir dispatches via a mass-conserving explainable AI (GBR-SHAP) topology; (ii) capturing the regulatory streamflow reshaping by extracting extreme quantiles (Q10, Q50, Q90) from empirical Flow Duration Curves (FDCs); (iii) quantifying the individual and interactive effects of climate and land-use on different subbasins using analysis of variance (ANOVA). The SHASE framework is applied to the “Ji"-shaped region of the Yellow River Basin. Key findings indicate: (1) GBR-SHAP feature sensitivities reveal empirical response patterns that align with known catchment moisture memory (dominated by 12-month rolling precipitation); (2) FDC analyses reveal an asymmetric flow-reshaping effect along the regulated channel, where reservoir operations truncate wet-season high flows (Q10) while supplementing dry-season low flows (Q90); (3) while climate change acts as the dominant macro-scale driver across more than 75% of the watershed (contributing over 76% of streamflow variance on average), urban surface hardening triggered high flow in 12.5% of the subbasins, while the interaction between climate and land use dominated the low-flow deficits in 20.0% of the subbasins during dry-season. The findings suggest that achieving sustainable watershed management requires a shift from isolated climate assessment to integrated climate-land-water coordination that addresses the local extreme-flow drivers in strictly regulated watersheds.

title: An efficient conditional diffusion model for meteorological data super-resolution based on stochastic differential equations over Eastern China
abstract: Global weather forecasts provide essential support for socioeconomic activities, but their applications remain constrained by coarse spatial resolution and systematic, regime-dependent biases, particularly over meteorologically heterogeneous regions. This study develops a conditional diffusion model based on stochastic differential equations, which integrates intensity-boundary structural learning with adaptive refinement via dynamic convolution and channel attention to produce high-resolution meteorological fields across multiple forecast products. Evaluations over Eastern China against ERA5-Land show that the super-resolution forecasts achieve strong agreement with the reference, with temperature and wind fields at a 12 h lead time reaching R2 values of up to about 0.90 and 0.87, respectively, and precipitation event skill reaching stable equitable error in probability space (SEEPS) values as low as approximately 0.05, consistently outperforming interpolation-based and deterministic learning methods. Compared with representative baseline models, the proposed framework demonstrates more robust performance across variables and forecast settings, with improved preservation of coherent spatial distributions, localized gradients, and extreme-value features. Using the super-resolution weather forecasts, we further demonstrate an application to gridded daily maximum 8 h ozone prediction. Compared with ozone predictions driven by the low-resolution meteorological fields, the use of super-resolved meteorological fields yields systematic improvements in predictive performance, with R2 increased by 4.6–5.8%. For the evaluated forecast products and meteorological variables over Eastern China, these results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective approach for regional-scale forecast refinement and downstream air-quality prediction.

title: Stakeholder-anchored multi-criteria deployment of island hybrid renewable energy systems for lifecycle carbon reduction: A weight-robustness analysis
abstract: Choosing a low-carbon configuration for an island hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) is a multi-criteria decision on which stakeholders disagree. This study ranks fourteen genetic-algorithm-sized HRES configurations for Crete on five composite criteria: economic, environmental, social, political and technological. The environmental criterion is the share of the grid's lifecycle carbon footprint a configuration avoids. Criterion weights are derived from a 100-respondent stakeholder survey by a Random Forest with its Shapley-value attribution (TreeSHAP) and by the model-free CRiteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) method, and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) ranks the configurations. The novelty is a diagnostic protocol that tests whether, and where, the recommendation depends on the weights: an equal-weights null, whole-simplex sampling, direct-rating and class-balanced weights, seven further aggregation methods, index-coefficient perturbation and a decision boundary. The marine-augmented configuration with battery storage (S14) ranks first under all three survey-based weightings and equal weights and, under the adopted inventory, avoids 79.15% of the grid's lifecycle carbon footprint, against 71.64% for the best shore-only option. This agreement stems mainly from the decision matrix, where S14 weakly dominates ten of thirteen alternatives. It leads in 67.0% of uniformly sampled weight vectors and under all seven further methods, but in only 57–77% of joint index-coefficient perturbations. Entropy weights, a higher political weight or a 20% higher policy premium for wind make a wind-rich alternative first. S14 is therefore the most frequent, not an invariant, first choice, conditional on policy judgements open to stakeholder deliberation.

title: Target dependent cleaner production screening of recycling pathways for end of life electric vehicle lithium ion batteries using an interpretable machine learning framework
abstract: Which recycling route is preferred when the decision target, proxy boundary, functional-unit scaling, and model-use domain change? This study developed an auditable, time-indexed scenario-screening framework for end-of-life electric-vehicle lithium-ion batteries. The deterministic grid contains 1008 designed combinations representing structured scenarios rather than plant observations. A prespecified 168-row subset of 84 paired physical configurations supported machine-learning (ML) evaluation. Six targets include process energy; operational energy-related CO2 burden limited to grid electricity and direct diesel/natural-gas combustion; a spend-proxy-credit-adjusted screening balance; and three mapped economic indicators. The adjusted balance subtracts spend-normalized recovered-material proxies from the narrower operational burden and serves as a screening indicator within this partial boundary. Pack values provide a cross-model mass-intensity sensitivity; a full pack-level life-cycle inventory lies outside the analysis. All 12 target-basis tasks used five-fold physical-configuration-grouped evaluation. For each task, grouped and route-held-out learners were selected separately by minimum mean root-mean-square error (RMSE). For adjusted balance, grouped RMSE and coefficient of determination (R2) values were 0.0816/0.99990 (cell) and 0.4561/0.99481 (pack); the corresponding lowest task-level route-held-out RMSEs were 7.0693 and 6.1501. Dependence-aware uncertainty analyses of the carbon-dioxide-equivalent (CO2e) indicators selected hydrometallurgical recycling for operational burden and direct recycling for fully credited adjusted balance under the specified screening assumptions. Removing the active-cathode spend proxy shifted the lower adjusted balance to hydrometallurgical recycling. Route preference changed across targets. The framework supports conditional screening and evidence prioritization within represented route families. Full life-cycle climate assessment requires complete inventories and verified substitution evidence. Application to a new route requires foreground data and revalidation.

title: Decoupling hydrological and economic drivers of global rainwater harvesting performance using explainable artificial intelligence
abstract: Decentralized rainwater harvesting (RWH) is critical for urban water resilience, yet current research remains fragmented, relying on site-specific case studies that limit the identification of transferable physical and economic patterns across heterogeneous urban contexts. Here, we present a unified, data-driven framework that harmonizes 3879 RWH cases across 179 cities into a globally consistent dataset. We developed predictive models for key economic and water-saving performance indicators, including benefit-cost ratio (BCR), Net Present Value (NPV), payback period (PBP), and water-saving efficiency (WSE). The predictive framework employs a Bayesian-optimized Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) integrated with interpretability algorithms. Model robustness was evaluated using random-split, study-isolated, and geographic extrapolation tests. Across the four targets, R2 values ranged from 0.928 to 0.960 under random split and 0.656–0.868 under study-isolated validation. Geographic transferability was scale-dependent: city-level extrapolation retained R2 values of 0.740–0.892, whereas country-level extrapolation declined markedly to 0.323–0.511. SHAP-based interpretation revealed nonlinear feature interactions and indicator-specific contribution patterns, with catchment fraction identified as a key predictor reflecting the influence of system scale matching between contributing area and harvesting capacity within the compiled dataset. These results support the framework as an interpretable screening and scenario-comparison tool within the climatic, socioeconomic, and system domains represented by the compiled dataset, while indicating that applications to substantially different national contexts require local calibration and additional validation.

title: Descriptor-resolved machine learning reveals response patterns and molecular interaction differences in MOF-based removal of hazardous aromatic pollutants
abstract: High adsorption capacities reported for MOF-based systems may reflect specific combinations of material, pollutant, and operating descriptors rather than transferable material performance. Here, a descriptor-resolved framework integrating literature-derived adsorption records, interpretable machine learning, sensitivity analysis, and representative molecular calculations was developed to distinguish response structure within the represented data domain from cross-publication transferability. The XGBoost model using CMAES-derived hyperparameters achieved a pooled out-of-fold R2 of 0.953 under record-level validation, whereas performance decreased markedly to R2 = −0.221 under publication-grouped validation. Despite this decline, the global descriptor-contribution hierarchy remained highly stable across the two validation schemes (ρ = 0.985), with initial concentration and adsorbent dosage ranking highest. Because both variables are mathematically linked to adsorption capacity, targeted feature-removal analysis was further performed. After simultaneously excluding them, the model retained an out-of-fold R2 of 0.854, while adsorption time, particle size, specific surface area, pore size, and pKa emerged as the highest-contributing descriptors. Representative paired response maps from the reduced model further revealed localized and non-monotonic associations among operating, material, and pollutant descriptors within the sampled domain. Molecular calculations showed that linker functionalization did not uniformly strengthen pollutant binding; instead, interaction stability depended on pollutant identity, aromatic contact, polar interaction, molecular orientation, and local linker chemistry. Overall, the framework distinguishes comparatively stable descriptor-response patterns from the more limited transferability of absolute adsorption-capacity predictions, providing a more rigorous basis for interpreting heterogeneous MOF adsorption evidence and prioritizing response patterns for independent experimental validation.
